text.p: The reorganisation of Banco Portugues de Investimento following the acquisition of Banco de Fomento e Exterior should be concluded by the end of 1998, BPI president Artur Santos Silva said.

"The reorganisation should be concluded 18 months to two years from the beginning of the consolidation in October 1996," Santos Silva told reporters after the presentation of the group's 1996 results on Wednesday.
BPI posted a 56 percent increase year-on-year in 1996 profits to 15.1 billion escudos.
The group would continue to operate in three areas -- investment banking, corporate banking and retail banking, Santos Silva said.
Santos Silva declined to say how many employees could take early retirement as part of the cost cutting programme under the restructuring.
"We have objectives (for early retirement), but we believe it is a process that should be carried out gradually, and that has to be agreed with each employee," he said.

After the purchase of BFE in August 1996, the group centralised the control of financial management, financial and credit risks, planning, and the auditing of the bank units of the group, Santos Silva said.
In Lisbon, the BPI group will save 600 million escudos a year in rent by leaving a building that housed BPI unit Banco Fonsecas & Burnay as part of the reorganisation, Santos Silva said.
The group will also save costs via the closure of a branch of BFE in Brussels. BFE branches in New York and Macau were also closed, Santos Silva said.
